sourceCitation: Real Decreto de 1884; Sistema de Cédulas Personales
lore: The Guardia Civil stops you at dusk outside the town plaza and demands identification. What do you present?

choices.text: Present your official paper Cédula Personal tax certificate.
Pull out a laminated Postal ID card from your modern wallet.
choices.cause: Accused of practicing witchcraft with demonic synthetic talismans and declared a vagamundo. You die of cholera in the colonial stockade.
choices.trivia: The 1884 Royal Decree replaced the tribute system with the mandatory paper Cédula Personal. Failing to produce valid paper documents resulted in immediate detention and hard labor.

choices.text: Slip the patrol officer a modern coin to discreetly let you pass.
choices.cause: Arrested on the spot for circulating illicit foreign currency and attempting to bribe colonial authorities. Summarily executed for treason.
choices.trivia: Colonial monetary laws strictly regulated currency circulation; possession of unauthorized coins or attempting to bribe the Guardia Civil carried severe penal penalties.

sourceCitation: Gaceta de Manila (1882); Archivo de la Real Audiencia
lore: Asiatic cholera sweeps through the parish. You feel severely dehydrated and need water immediately. What is your course of action?

choices.text: Boil well water thoroughly inside your quarters and remain strictly within parish quarantine cordons.
Drink cool river water from the Pasig to quickly rehydrate after fleeing the cordon.
choices.cause: Contracted acute Asiatic cholera from municipal contamination and perished within twelve hours.
choices.trivia: The 1882 cholera epidemic devastated Manila due to contaminated river and shallow well water; boiling water was one of the few effective survival methods.

choices.text: Attempt to cross the armed river barricade after evening curfew to seek a clinic.
choices.cause: Shot on sight by the Guardia Civil enforcing the lethal sanitary cordon around the arrabal.
choices.trivia: Quarantine cordons were military checkpoints where sentries were authorized to use lethal force against anyone breaking night curfews.

sourceCitation: Catálogo Alfabético de Apellidos (1849), Archivo Histórico Nacional
lore: Governor-General Clavería decrees the standardization of surnames. You are summoned by the Cabeza de Barangay to register your household. What name do you provide?

choices.text: Accept an assigned surname selected directly from the official Catálogo Alfabético.
Insist on giving your real 21st-century hyphenated legal name and claim you are already registered in civil registries.
choices.cause: Deemed mentally deranged and a subversive agitator resisting colonial governance. Exiled to hard labor in the Cavite naval arsenals.
choices.trivia: The 1849 Clavería decree ended arbitrary indigenous naming practices to fix tribute evasion; refusal to accept cataloged surnames was punished as civil rebellion.

choices.text: Refuse to register entirely, asserting constitutional rights to privacy.
choices.cause: Classified as an uncataloged outlaw (tulisán) and sentenced to penal servitude in Guam.
choices.trivia: Unregistered individuals were stripped of legal status, branded as vagabonds or bandits, and faced indefinite penal exile.

sourceCitation: Bando de Guerra del Gobernador General Blanco (Agosto 1896)
lore: Martial law is declared across eight provinces. Guardia Civil patrols conduct warrantless midnight house searches for Katipunan paraphernalia. How do you prepare?

choices.text: Burn suspicious private correspondences, securely conceal modern items, and ensure your Cédula is stamped.
Film the Guardia Civil search on your smartphone to document human rights abuses.
choices.cause: Your device is seized as an instrument of black sorcery and treason. Summarily executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan.
choices.trivia: During the 1896 crackdown, suspected subversives caught with unexplained items or writings faced immediate drumhead court-martials.

choices.text: Keep printed pocket pamphlets in an unlocked chest, planning to explain civil liberties to the inspecting officer.
choices.cause: Arrested on treason charges as an active Katipunan conspirator and condemned to death in Fort Santiago dungeons.
choices.trivia: Possession of any coded letters, masonic emblems, or unauthorized circulars during martial law resulted in summary execution.

sourceCitation: Leyes de Indias; Polo y Servicios Reales
lore: The local Alcalde Mayor drafts all native males into polo y servicio for 40 days of timber cutting to supply the Manila Galleon shipyards. How do you respond?

choices.text: Pay the official falla fee in silver or report for log-hauling labor with your tools.
Quote international labor laws and demand compensation for involuntary servitude.
choices.cause: Publicly flogged 50 lashes for sedition and chained to an oar on a colonial galley ship.
choices.trivia: Polo y servicio was mandatory corvée labor for male natives aged 16 to 60. Refusal without paying the steep exemption tax (falla) was treated as rebellion.

choices.text: Flee to the forested mountains without tribute clearance.
choices.cause: Branded a remontado rebel and hunted down by Spanish indigenous tracker battalions.
choices.trivia: Fleeing polo labor placed individuals outside colonial law, making them subject to capture and lifelong enslavement.

sourceCitation: Manual Parroquial; Reglas Eclesiásticas de Filipinas
lore: At 6:00 PM, the church bells begin ringing the Angelus across the town plaza while you are walking. What do you do?

choices.text: Halt immediately, remove your hat, kneel or bow your head, and recite the prayer.
Keep walking quickly toward your destination while wearing headphones.
choices.cause: Spotted by the parish fiscal, struck with a rattan cane for public blasphemy, and imprisoned in the parish carcel.
choices.trivia: Stopping and bowing for the Angelus was strictly enforced by church fiscals; ignoring the bells was considered an explicit act of heresy.

choices.text: Argue with the parish curate about freedom of religion and separation of church and state.
choices.cause: Turned over to the Holy Office of the Inquisition and condemned to penal galley labor.
choices.trivia: The Catholic Church held extensive civic authority in the colonies; denying church supremacy resulted in severe inquisitorial punishment.

sourceCitation: Reglamento del Real Consulado de Manila
lore: The Acapulco Galleon has arrived in port. A foreign merchant offers you speculative boleta shares to claim silk and porcelain cargo without a royal permit. How do you act?

choices.text: Decline the deal and conduct all currency and trade exchanges exclusively through the authorized Real Consulado.
Attempt to transfer modern digital funds or issue a private handwritten promissory note for cargo space.
choices.cause: Charged with fraudulent counterfeiting and high treason against the Royal Treasury. Sentenced to hard labor in the Marianas.
choices.trivia: Galleon cargo space was strictly rationed via royal boletas issued only to favored Spanish residents, widows, and clergy.

choices.text: Purchase the unregistered boletas and attempt to sell the Chinese silk directly out of a street stall.
choices.cause: Goods confiscated by the Real Aduana; convicted of contraband trade and sent to penal servitude.
choices.trivia: Unregistered galleon cargo trade was heavily prosecuted to preserve the crown's monopoly on Mexican silver exchange.

sourceCitation: Sistema de Bandala; Crónicas Coloniales de Filipinas
lore: Crown officials arrive to requisition your entire rice harvest under the Bandala system, offering promissory paper notes that will take years to redeem. What do you do?

choices.text: Surrender the required quota of grain and retain the royal promissory receipt.
Threaten to file a consumer protection lawsuit against the crown for unfair trade practices.
choices.cause: Strung up on the plaza gallows as an instigator of agrarian revolt against the Spanish Crown.
choices.trivia: The Bandala forced-sale quota system frequently drove provinces into near-famine and sparked major revolts like the Maniago Uprising of 1660.

choices.text: Burn down the granary so Spanish officials cannot seize your harvest.
choices.cause: Convicted of economic sabotage against the Real Hacienda and garroted in the town square.
choices.trivia: Destroying crops to evade the Bandala levy was punished by public execution and confiscation of all family properties.

sourceCitation: Leyes de Indias: De las clases y trajes
lore: You prepare to pass through the gates into Intramuros. What attire do you wear?

choices.text: Wear an untucked sheer baro made of piña fiber without pockets and carry your travel pass.
Wear a modern European tailored wool suit with tucked-in shirt and necktie.
choices.cause: Arrested at the gate for violating sumptuary caste regulations and impersonating a Peninsular noble.
choices.trivia: Colonial dress codes required natives to keep their shirts untucked and transparent without pockets to prevent weapons concealment and mark social hierarchy.

choices.text: Walk through the gate wearing modern sunglasses and jeans, ignoring the gate guards.
choices.cause: Struck down with halberds by the Puerta Real sentries for failing to uncover your head and bow.
choices.trivia: Entering Intramuros required natives to show deferential posture, remove head coverings, and present valid passes.

sourceCitation: Estatutos de Limpieza de Sangre; Archivo Arquidiocesano
lore: You apply for a clerk position at a royal administrative tribunal and are asked to prove your purity of blood (limpieza de sangre). How do you answer?

choices.text: Present certified baptismal records from your local parish confirming legitimate Christian ancestry.
Hand them a printed DNA test certificate showing your ancestral ethnic percentages.
choices.cause: Denounced for using alchemical sorcery documents; arrested by the Inquisition for occult fraud.
choices.trivia: Colonial bureaucracies only accepted formal ecclesiastical lineage records signed by parish priests to verify blood purity and orthodoxy.

choices.text: Declare that all races are equal under secular human rights declarations.
choices.cause: Condemned as a radical French Enlightenment subversive and sentenced to lifelong exile in Mindanao.
choices.trivia: Egalitarian philosophy was fiercely suppressed in Spanish territories following the 1789 French Revolution.

sourceCitation: Reglamento de la Real Expedición Filantrópica de la Vacuna
lore: The Royal Balmis Expedition arrives with the live smallpox vaccine. You develop a mild rash and officials arrive at your home. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Submit to inspection by the municipal protomédico and accept quarantine or vaccination.
Pop modern antibiotic tablets from your bag in front of the physicians and refuse isolation.
choices.cause: Accused of ingesting lethal witch powders; detained indefinitely in the asylum wards of San Lazaro.
choices.trivia: Colonial medical authorities were deeply suspicious of unvetted concoctions, viewing unknown pills as either poisons or sorcery.

choices.text: Bribe the health inspector with modern dollar bills to falsify your health certificate.
choices.cause: Imprisoned for counterfeiting worthless non-metallic currency and violating public sanitation laws.
choices.trivia: Paper bank notes had no legal tender status in the early 19th-century Philippines, where silver real and peso coins were paramount.

sourceCitation: Sumaria sobre la Sublevación de Cavite de 1872
lore: Artillery workers mutiny at Fort San Felipe after Governor-General Izquierdo strips their tax exemption. Soldiers knock on your workshop door demanding allegiance. What do you do?

choices.text: Barricade your shop, remain completely silent indoors, and avoid signing any petitions or documents.
Step into the square with a megaphone to organize a peaceful labor mediation committee.
choices.cause: Executed immediately by Spanish marine infantry retaking the fort without trial.
choices.trivia: The 1872 Cavite Mutiny was suppressed with ruthless force, leading to widespread summary executions and the garrote execution of Gomburza.

choices.text: Sign the rebel manifestos believing you can plead worker immunity in civic court later.
choices.cause: Sentenced to capital execution for high treason against the Spanish Crown.
choices.trivia: Anyone associated with the mutineers' petitions was rounded up, subjected to military courts, and either executed or exiled to the Marianas.

sourceCitation: Informes de la Guardia Civil sobre Bandolerismo
lore: Your transport cart is ambushed on a remote pass by armed tulisán bandits wielding machetes and flintlocks. How do you react?

choices.text: Surrender your physical baggage, keep your eyes downcast, and offer no armed resistance.
Reach for your pocket pepper spray to incapacitate the bandit leader.
choices.cause: Hacked down instantly by accompanying bandits before you can discharge the canister.
choices.trivia: Colonial highwaymen (tulisanes) operated in large, lethal gangs along provincial trade roads; resisting without firearms was almost invariably fatal.

choices.text: Tell them police GPS tracking is already monitoring your position.
choices.cause: Taken hostage, tortured for explanations of invisible tracking demons, and killed when no ransom arrives.
choices.trivia: Bandits rarely kept captives alive if ransom or immediate compliance was not secured promptly.

sourceCitation: Relación del Terremoto de Manila de 1863
lore: A catastrophic earthquake hits during Corpus Christi eve. Masonry crashes down from the Manila Cathedral. Where do you take shelter?

choices.text: Flee immediately into the center of the open plaza away from stone walls and heavy tile roofs.
Run inside the cathedral seeking sanctuary beneath the massive stone dome.
choices.cause: Crushed when the cathedral's heavy stone roof and bell towers collapsed entirely into the nave.
choices.trivia: The 1863 Manila earthquake flattened the Manila Cathedral and the Governor's Palace, killing hundreds sheltered inside stone structures.

choices.text: Climb up to the balcony of a nearby multi-story stone bahay-na-bato to film the collapse.
choices.cause: Perished when the upper brick walls collapsed into the street.
choices.trivia: Spanish-era unreinforced stone buildings were notorious death traps during seismic events before wood-frame earthquake designs were adopted.

sourceCitation: Bando de Expulsión del Gobernador Simón de Anda y Salazar
lore: During the British occupation of Manila, Spanish forces under Simón de Anda order all trade with non-Spanish merchants halted under pain of death. What do you do?

choices.text: Relocate strictly to loyalist Spanish zones in Bacolor, Pampanga, and observe strict military curfews.
Set up a black-market trading stand between British soldiers and local Parian merchants.
choices.cause: Captured by Anda's loyalist guerrillas and hanged as an economic collaborator with the British.
choices.trivia: Simón de Anda declared martial law against any residents collaborating with British occupation forces or trade networks.

choices.text: Wave a white flag and declare yourself an internationally protected neutral civilian.
choices.cause: Cut down in the crossfire during the Spanish counter-offensive against the British-held bastions.
choices.trivia: The Geneva Conventions did not exist in the 18th century; civilians caught between besieging forces received no formal legal protections.

sourceCitation: Instrucciones de Cobranza del Real Tributo
lore: The tribute collector arrives at your village. You must pay your semestral tribute of 8 silver reales. What tender do you provide?

choices.text: Hand over official Spanish silver pillar dollars (reales) or accepted agricultural produce in kind.
Attempt to pay using modern plastic credit cards or polymer banknotes.
choices.cause: Denounced for attempting to defraud the Real Hacienda with cursed artificial slips; sentenced to the pillory.
choices.trivia: Tribute was strictly calculated in silver reales or official commodities like rice, wax, and cotton cloth according to royal tariff tables.

choices.text: Offer copper buttons and claim they are fractional digital fiat tokens.
choices.cause: Convicted of counterfeiting royal currency and sentenced to 100 lashes and mining labor.
choices.trivia: Counterfeiting or debasing coinage was considered an offense against the crown's sovereign person, punishable by mutilation or execution.

sourceCitation: Comisión Permanente de Censura de Manila
lore: You are arriving on a steamship from Hong Kong carrying a package containing Jose Rizal's *Noli Me Tángere*. Port censors board for an inspection. What do you do?

choices.text: Secretly drop the package into the sea before the inspection team reaches your berth.
Show the inspector the book while citing constitutional freedom of speech and the press.
choices.cause: Arrested on the spot by the Permanent Commission of Censorship for high treason and subversion.
choices.trivia: The Permanent Commission of Censorship strictly banned Rizal's novels; possession carried immediate penal exile or imprisonment.

choices.text: Offer to sell copies of the novel to fellow passengers on the open deck.
choices.cause: Reported by an undercover informant; condemned to indefinite incarceration in the penal colony of Puerto Princesa.
choices.trivia: The Spanish administration utilized extensive networks of paid informers (confidentes) in Manila ports to intercept forbidden texts.

sourceCitation: Relación de las Encomiendas en las Islas Filipinas (1591)
lore: The Spanish encomendero demands an excessive tribute of gold dust and woven textiles that exceeds the legal tasa. How do you handle the demand?

choices.text: Appeal formally through your Christian parish missionary friar to lodge a grievance with the Bishop.
Physically attack the encomendero with a farm scythe in front of his soldiers.
choices.cause: Hacked down immediately by the encomendero's arquebusiers and display-hung from a mango tree.
choices.trivia: Early encomenderos possessed private military authority; armed rebellion against an encomendero resulted in swift retributive executions.

choices.text: Demand to see the encomendero's corporate tax license and threat to audit him.
choices.cause: Put in irons as an insolent pagan and worked to death in the gold placer mines.
choices.trivia: Ecclesiastical authorities (like Bishop Domingo de Salazar) were often the only legal restraint on abusive encomenderos in the 16th century.

sourceCitation: Reglamento para el Servicio de Serenos y Guardia Civil Veterana
lore: The night watchman (sereno) cries midnight. You are caught on the street without a lantern after the curfew bell. How do you respond?

choices.text: Extinguish your light, freeze in place, and calmly surrender to the sereno for identification.
Turn on your smartphone flashlight and shine it directly into the night watchman's eyes.
choices.cause: Mistaken for a demonic shapeshifter (aswang) bearing hellfire; speared through by the responding night patrol.
choices.trivia: Colonial ordinances required anyone moving at night to carry a lit candle or oil lantern; unexplainable blinding lights triggered panic and violence.

choices.text: Run away through the dark alleys to evade questioning.
choices.cause: Shot dead by a Guardia Civil Veterana sentry enforcing night anti-banditry regulations.
choices.trivia: Sentries had standing orders to fire upon anyone who fled when challenged with '¿Quién vive?' after the final curfew bell.

sourceCitation: Causa del Comisario del Santo Oficio de Manila
lore: A neighbor denounces you to the Inquisitorial Commissioner for muttering unfamiliar words in English and not attending confession. What is your defense?

choices.text: Present witnesses affirming your daily participation in the Mass and recite the Creed in Spanish.
Explain that you are an agnostic humanist who values science over dogma.
choices.cause: Condemned as a relapsed formal heretic; paraded in a sanbenito robe and sentenced to life imprisonment.
choices.trivia: Openly professing agnosticism or denying Catholic dogma before the Inquisition resulted in severe canonical penalties and property confiscation.

choices.text: Attempt to educate the tribunal on evolutionary biology and astrophysics.
choices.cause: Burned at the stake in an auto-da-fé for unrepentant demonic apostasy.
choices.trivia: Challenging core biblical cosmology before ecclesiastical tribunals was treated as direct heresy against church doctrine.

sourceCitation: Reglamento General del Estanco de Tabaco
lore: Revenue guards (resguardos) inspect your farm. They discover three unregistered tobacco plants growing behind your garden shed. What do you do?

choices.text: Immediately uproot the plants, pay the administrative fine, and pledge all harvest to the monopoly.
Roll the tobacco into cigarettes and offer to sell them directly to the guards at wholesale rates.
choices.cause: Arrested for contraband trade under the Tobacco Monopoly; sentenced to 10 years hard labor in the Bilibid prison.
choices.trivia: The Tobacco Monopoly (1782–1882) strictly prohibited private curing, possession, or sale of tobacco under extreme penalties.

choices.text: Claim the plants are for medical personal use protected under modern herbal regulations.
choices.cause: Farm razed to the ground; condemned to penal servitude for illegal plantation cultivation.
choices.trivia: No private exceptions existed under the Estanco de Tabaco; unauthorized farming led to land confiscation and corporal punishment.

year: 1896 — El Polvorín, San Juan del Monte
sourceCitation: Partes Oficiales de Operaciones Militares (1896)
lore: Katipunan forces assault the Spanish powder magazine (El Polvorín). You find yourself trapped in the combat zone as Spanish reinforcements arrive. What do you do?

choices.text: Conceal yourself in a drainage culvert without weapons until all gunfire and sweeps cease.
Pick up a discarded bolo and charge the Spanish artillery line to join the attack.
choices.cause: Cut down by rapid-fire Mauser volleys from arriving Spanish reinforcements at the Battle of Pinaglabanan.
choices.trivia: The Battle of San Juan del Monte resulted in catastrophic insurgent casualties due to the firepower advantage of Spanish Mauser rifles.

choices.text: Step into the road shouting for a ceasefire so you can photograph the historical event.
choices.cause: Shot dead instantly by Spanish infantry skirmish lines clearing the perimeter.
choices.trivia: Spanish troops operated under strict orders to eliminate anyone in the combat theater without uniforms or passes.

sourceCitation: Crónicas de la Rebelión de Dagohoy en Bohol
lore: Francisco Dagohoy establishes an independent settlement in the Bohol mountains after a Jesuit priest refuses his brother Christian burial. You are traveling near the rebel lines. How do you proceed?

choices.text: Maintain strict neutrality, follow established mountain trails, and state your peaceful travel intent.
Wear a Spanish military insignia hoping it will intimidate the mountain sentries.
choices.cause: Ambushed and speared by Dagohoy's sentries as a colonial spy for the Spanish authorities.
choices.trivia: The Dagohoy Rebellion lasted 85 years; rebel communities ruthlessly hunted anyone bearing Spanish military or administrative marks.

choices.text: Attempt to lecture the rebels on the legal supremacy of Spanish provincial court systems.
choices.cause: Executed by the rebel council for colluding with colonial oppressors.
choices.trivia: The Bohol rebels formed an autonomous government that rejected all Spanish administrative and religious sovereignty.

sourceCitation: El Proceso de los Padres Gómez, Burgos y Zamora
lore: Fathers Gómez, Burgos, and Zamora have just been executed by garrote before thousands of silent onlookers. Spanish cavalry patrols closely monitor the dispersing crowd. How do you leave?

choices.text: Keep your head down, maintain utter silence, and walk directly home with the crowd.
Start a public chant demanding justice and immediate democratic reforms.
choices.cause: Trampled and sabered by Spanish cavalry clearing the execution grounds of agitators.
choices.trivia: The atmosphere following the 1872 execution was intensely volatile; any public vocal protest was met with instant military violence.

choices.text: Take notes on paper about the executions to publish an op-ed article.
choices.cause: Arrested by undercover secret police (policía secreta) and charged with treasonous sedition.
choices.trivia: Writers and journalists documenting political dissent were monitored by colonial secret police and faced immediate exile.

sourceCitation: Pacto de Biak-na-Bato; Archivo de la Capitanía General
lore: The revolutionary leadership signs the Pact of Biak-na-Bato, agreeing to a truce and exile to Hong Kong. Spanish couriers prepare the surrender amnesty lists. How do you finalize your 30th shift?

choices.text: Present yourself under the formal amnesty registry, surrender weapons, and complete the time shift.
Denounce the truce as a financial sellout and attempt to single-handedly attack the Spanish negotiating team.
choices.cause: Shot dead by both revolutionary security and Spanish sentries guarding the truce negotiations.
choices.trivia: The Pact of Biak-na-Bato provided conditional amnesty to registered revolutionaries; rogue attackers were eliminated by both sides.

choices.text: Attempt to broker a modern United Nations intervention treaty between both parties.
choices.cause: Declared an unhinged spy and executed in the mountain redoubt.
choices.trivia: Modern international bodies had no historical counterpart in 1897; unauthorized foreign mediators were treated as spies.

sourceCitation: Historical treatment of hydrophobia before Pasteur's rabies vaccine (1885)
lore: A stray dog behaving strangely bites you deeply on the leg before disappearing. A neighbor warns that the animal may be suffering from hydrophobia. What do you do?

choices.text: Go to confession and receive penance in case the illness proves fatal.
choices.cause: The bite heals. Weeks later, fever and agitation begin, followed by agonizing spasms whenever you attempt to drink. Your penance prepared your soul, but not your body. You die of hydrophobia.
choices.trivia: Rabies was commonly called hydrophobia because victims developed painful spasms when attempting to swallow liquids. Before Pasteur's rabies vaccine in 1885, there was no reliable cure once symptoms appeared.

choices.text: Go immediately to the nearest physician and have the wound cleaned and cauterized with a hot iron.
Wash the wound thoroughly and dress it with boiled guava leaves to prevent infection.
choices.cause: The wound heals cleanly, but the unseen disease does not. Weeks later, you develop violent throat spasms and hydrophobia. Once the symptoms appear, nothing available in 1847 can save you.
choices.trivia: Traditional wound treatments could address the injury itself, but they could not reliably prevent rabies. Physicians before Pasteur sometimes attempted immediate cleansing, excision, or cauterization of suspicious animal bites.

sourceCitation: History of dentistry before modern antibiotics
lore: A tooth that has been aching for days is now badly swollen. Your cheek is hot, the pain is spreading into your jaw, and you are beginning to feel feverish. What do you do?

choices.text: Have the infected tooth pulled as soon as possible.
Go to the botica and ask for antibiotics.
choices.cause: The boticario has no idea what medicine you are asking for. While you search for antibiotics that will not exist for decades, the infection spreads through your jaw and neck. You die from the uncontrolled infection.
choices.trivia: Antibiotics did not exist in 1871. Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928, and effective antibiotic treatment became widely available much later.

choices.text: Chew betel nut and drink lambanog to dull the pain until the swelling goes down.
choices.cause: The pain becomes easier to tolerate. The infection does not. It spreads beyond the tooth and into the surrounding tissues until fever and swelling overwhelm you.
choices.trivia: Before antibiotics, relieving dental pain did not eliminate the source of a serious tooth infection. Extraction and drainage were among the limited ways of removing the source of infection.

sourceCitation: Nineteenth-century provincial travel and banditry in the Philippines
lore: You must reach the next pueblo before nightfall. Locals warn that tulisanes have recently been attacking travelers after dark. You have no watch. When do you leave?

choices.text: At midday. There should still be several hours of daylight.
choices.cause: You badly underestimate the journey by carabao. Darkness falls while you are still far from the next pueblo. Tulisanes find you on the road. Your carabao returns alone the following morning. You are never seen again.
choices.trivia: Travel between pueblos could take hours over difficult provincial roads. Without modern transportation or personal timekeeping, daylight and communal signals such as church bells were important guides for travelers.

choices.text: Immediately after the morning church bells.
In the early afternoon, when the heat begins to ease.
choices.cause: The cooler journey is considerably more pleasant. It is also your last. Night falls before you reach the pueblo. Your carabao is found wandering along the road the next morning. You are never seen again.
choices.trivia: Tulisanes and other bandit groups were a persistent problem on isolated provincial roads during the nineteenth century, making travel after dark considerably more dangerous.

sourceCitation: Historical accounts of the Pasig River and nineteenth-century Manila
lore: The afternoon heat is unbearable. The Pasig River looks remarkably clean compared with the river you remember from the present day. You need a bath. What do you do?

choices.text: Jump into the Pasig and enjoy the surprisingly clean water.
choices.cause: You have sufficiently fed a crocodile.
choices.trivia: Crocodiles historically inhabited Philippine rivers and waterways, including waterways around Manila. A cleaner-looking nineteenth-century river was not necessarily a harmless place for recreational swimming.

choices.text: Draw water from a well and bathe at home.
Go farther upstream, away from the crowded city, and bathe where the current is stronger.
choices.cause: The current is considerably stronger than it looks. You are swept downstream and drown before anyone can reach you.
choices.trivia: The Pasig was an important transportation and everyday-use waterway. River conditions, currents, boats, and wildlife created hazards that a modern visitor could easily underestimate.

sourceCitation: Late Spanish colonial accounts of parish friars and municipal politics
lore: The parish friar invites you to dine at the convento. During dinner, he begins complaining bitterly about the gobernadorcillo and asks what you think of him. What do you do?

choices.text: Agree enthusiastically and tell the friar everything you have heard about the gobernadorcillo.
choices.cause: By morning, the gobernadorcillo has somehow heard every word you said. You discover too late that becoming involved in a feud between the pueblo's two most powerful men was not an effective survival strategy.
choices.trivia: Parish friars could exercise substantial influence in local political and social affairs, while municipal officials possessed their own networks of allies and dependents. Navigating those relationships required considerable caution.

choices.text: Politely avoid taking sides and redirect the conversation to something harmless.
Defend the gobernadorcillo and explain that matters of government should remain separate from the Church.
choices.cause: You have successfully explained the separation of Church and State to the friar. At the garrote, you learn fraylology.
choices.trivia: Fraylology was a satirical way of describing the practical art of understanding and navigating the influence, personalities, and politics of the Spanish friars in colonial Philippine society.
